entries.title: Daniel 3:1
segments:
Of gold; probably so called because it was overlaid with gold. 
 
vv 1-23. 
 
Since rulers are ordained of God, we are bound to submit ourselves to all their requirements, except when they command that which God forbids, or forbid that which God commands; and then we must obey God, though it be at the peril of our lives.

entries.title: Daniel 3:2
segments: Sheriffs; rather, "men learned in the law."

entries.title: Daniel 3:5
segments:
Sackbut; the original word seems to denote a stringed instrument like the lyre. 
 
  Ye fall down and worship; this was in accordance with the universal belief of heathen nations, that it belonged to the state to regulate the worship of the gods.  Of the rights of conscience they had no clear ideas.

entries.title: Daniel 3:16
segments: Are not careful; or, "have no need."  Their minds were made up to refuse the worship demanded of them, and they knew that arguing the matter would do no good.

entries.title: Daniel 3:21
segments: Their coats--garments; or, "their hosen, tunics, mantles, and garments."  "Hosen" are wide pantaloons, such as are worn now in eastern countries.

entries.title: Daniel 3:24
segments:
vv 24-28. 
 
God is able with infinite ease to deliver his servants in the most terrible extremities.  Though he may not see good to save their bodies from present death, as he did those of Daniel's three companions, he will grant to their spirits a perfect triumph over the rage of their enemies; and "in the resurrection at the last day" he will restore their bodies also in a glorified state, so that throughout eternity they shall "have no hurt" from the wicked, in body or soul.

entries.title: Daniel 3:25
segments: Like the Son of God; or, "like a son of the gods," that is, a superhuman being.  The same personage Nebuchadnezzar afterwards calls an "angel,"
